items.titleTr: Surgeon having lunch near Krakow shooting undoubtedly saved officer's life, colleague says
items.summaryTr: Further details have emerged about two police officers hailed for preventing a Polish gunman from killing more.
items.articleText: Surgeon having lunch near Krakow shooting undoubtedly saved officer's life, colleague says - Published One of two surgeons who treated victims on the streets in the aftermath of a mass shooting in Krakow, Poland said his colleague"undoubtedly" saved the life of a gravely injured police officer. The pair were eating near the city's Main Market Square on Saturday when a gunman began firing at random, killing six and injuring 15. The doctors raced to treat both the attacker and two officers shot while subduing the perpetrator. On Sunday, the officers - both hailed as "true heroes" by the prime minister for preventing further deaths - emerged from comas. Prosecutors launched a terror investigation after ministers previously said the 24-year-old Polish attacker - who remains in a critical condition - was apparently inspired by "far-right ideologies". A British national and Austrian woman were among those killed alongside four Poles. Professor Michal Pędziwiatr and Dr Mateusz Wierdak were having lunch in central Krakow with their families when they heard gunshots, local media reported. "Suddenly my son ran up and said: 'Dad, they're shooting at people there, people are falling to the ground'," Pędziwiatr told news outlet Fakt. Pędziwiatr said when they got to the scene, they treated both the apparent attacker and the police officers. "When it comes to saving lives, it doesn't matter who is who," he added. Once the shooting stopped, Pędziwiatr said he took care of the other victims and the perpetrator, while Wierdak began working on the police officer who was shot in the chest during the gunfight. "He, to put it colloquially, stuffed all the bandages into [the police officer's] chest and stuck his hands in," he told Fakt. "If not for that, I don't know how things would have turned out, as there was a long wait for the ambulance." Meanwhile, Pędziwiatr said he called John Paul II Hospital where the Department of Thoracic and Cardiac Surgery is located. "I insisted they take him there because, in my opinion, he had the best chance of survival there, where there were specialists for precisely this type of injury," he told Fakt. According to local media, Wierdak is a renowned surgeon in Krakow. The University Hospital in Krakow states Pędziwiatr is head of General, Oncological, Metabolic and Emergency Surgery. The police officers have been identified as senior constables Jakub Kulik and Artur Morański. The attacker has not yet been named by authorities. When his house was searched after the attack in central Krakow, the bodies of his parents and sister were found. The National Public Prosecutor's Office in Poland launched an investigation into the attack with a unit specialising in "terrorist offences" taking the lead. Separately, reports emerged that six Dublin Civil Defence volunteers also assisted in the aftermath of the shooting. James McConnell, an officer, told RTE News the group were on a city break and were close to the main square, external when the shooting happened. The volunteers who are trained to provide medical care immediately sought to help injured people, providing "CPR and haemorrhage control". Witnesses who were close to the attack described panic and confusion around the square as it unfolded. Ruby Catherine Warren, from London, heard gunfire and "yelled at my friends to run and we all sprinted for our lives". Not knowing where the gunman was - or if there was more than one - they "just kept sprinting", eventually finding a hotel to hide inside. Tom Brook, from West Yorkshire, was inside a McDonald's near the square when he heard "multiple gunshots and saw people running for cover". "I then walked into the square and saw paramedics working on someone outside [a shop] and there was a dead body covered in foil blankets 20 meters away," he said. The suspect wore full military tactical gear during the attack and was described as having a military-grade weapon - but the government said he was not a member of the Polish armed forces. Poland's Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński said "everything suggests" the suspect was "fascinated by far-right ideologies" and held ultra-nationalist views. The rampage began shortly before 15:00 local time (14:00 GMT) on Saturday in the historic centre of Krakow. Footage showed the attacker's vehicle speeding through the centre of the city, and people fleeing as the sound of gunfire rang out. The glass fronts of shops were shattered by bullets and a tram was shot at during the attack, which police say lasted for around three minutes. The mayor of Krakow said he had submitted an urgent request for the two officers injured while stopping the attacker to be awarded titles of honorary citizens of the city. Main Market Square reopened on Sunday evening after a security cordon was lifted. - Published7 hours ago - Published8 hours ago - Published1 day ago - Published1 day ago

items.title: Trump'tan İran savaşında sürpriz hamle: Devreye Çin girdi
items.summary: ABD Başkanı Donald Trump yönetiminin, İran'la savaşı sona erdirmek için Çin'den yardım istediği öne sürüldü. Washington Post'un haberine göre Pekin, ABD'nin mesajını Tahran'a iletirken, Trump'ın Şi Cinping ile yapacağı görüşmede İran konusunun ele alınması bekleniyor.

items.articleText: Trump'tan İran savaşında sürpriz hamle: Devreye Çin girdi - ABD Başkanı Donald Trump yönetiminin, İran'la savaşı sona erdirmek için Çin'den yardım istediği öne sürüldü. Washington Post'un haberine göre Pekin, ABD'nin mesajını Tahran'a iletirken, Trump'ın Şi Cinping ile yapacağı görüşmede İran konusunun ele alınması bekleniyor. Washington Post (WP) gazetesinin ABD'li ve Avrupalı yetkililere dayandırdığı habere göre, ABD'de savaşa yönelik kamuoyu tepkisinin artması, Trump yönetimini diplomatik çözüm arayışlarını hızlandırmaya yöneltti. İran'la savaşın sona erdirilmesi, yönetimin karşı karşıya olduğu en acil ve zorlu meselelerden biri olarak değerlendiriliyor. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Haberde, ABD Hazine Bakanı Scott Bessent'in Trump'ın desteğiyle Çin hükümetiyle temasa geçtiği belirtildi. Bessent'in, Pekin yönetiminden İran üzerindeki nüfuzunu kullanarak savaşın sona erdirilmesine katkıda bulunmasını istediği öne sürüldü. Çin'in de ABD'den gelen mesajı Tahran yönetimine ilettiği iddia edildi. Gözler 18 Kasım'daki görüşmede Diplomatik temasların sürdüğü bir dönemde, Trump'ın 18 Kasım'da Çin'de Devlet Başkanı Şi Cinping ile gerçekleştirmesi planlanan görüşmede İran meselesinin de gündeme gelmesi bekleniyor. Görüşmeye Rusya Devlet Başkanı Vladimir Putin'in de katılabileceği iddia edilirken, üç liderin aynı masada buluşup buluşmayacağına ilişkin henüz resmi bir açıklama yapılmadı. Öte yandan Çin'in Orta Doğu Özel Temsilcisi Büyükelçi Cay Cün'ün de savaşın sona erdirilmesine yönelik diplomatik girişimler kapsamında İran, Umman ve Suudi Arabistan'ı ziyaret etmesi bekleniyor.

items.articleText: Shaquille O'Neal'dan iflasa karşı emeklilik planı: Her ay 1 milyon dolar alacak! NBA efsanesi Shaquille O'Neal, servetini kaybetme ihtimaline karşı yıllar önce yaptığı yatırımı açıkladı. Ünlü basketbolcu, 55 yaşından itibaren emeklilik gelir sigortası sayesinde ayda yaklaşık 1 milyon dolar gelir elde etmeyi beklediğini söyledi. Basketbol tarihinin en tanınmış isimlerinden Shaquille O'Neal, milyonlarca dolarlık servetini nasıl koruduğunu ve gelecekteki gelirini nasıl güvence altına aldığını anlattı. "Dinner Party" podcast'ine konuk olan dört NBA şampiyonluğu sahibi eski basketbolcu, genç yaşta kazandığı büyük paraları harcama alışkanlığından nasıl vazgeçtiğini ve yıllar önce aldığı finansal kararların bugün kendisine nasıl bir güvence sağladığını paylaştı. O'Neal, yatırımlarının başarısız olması veya servetini kaybetmesi ihtimaline karşı kazancının önemli bir bölümünü düzenli gelir sağlayan emeklilik ürünlerine yönlendirdiğini söyledi. Ünlü basketbolcu, bu yatırımlar sayesinde gelecek yıl 55 yaşına geldiğinde aylık yaklaşık 1 milyon dolar gelir elde etmeyi beklediğini açıkladı. Zengin bir adamın peçeteyle verdiği ders hayatını değiştirdi O'Neal'ın finansal yaklaşımının değişmesinde yıllar önce tanıştığı varlıklı bir kişinin önemli rolü oldu. Ünlü basketbolcu, lüks otomobillere ve gösterişli bir yaşam tarzına sahip olan bu kişiye servetini nasıl koruyabileceğini sorduğunu anlattı. Aldığı yanıt ise oldukça basitti. Zengin iş insanı, bir peçeteyi önce ikiye, ardından tekrar ikiye bölerek parasını dört parçaya ayırması gerektiğini gösterdi. O'Neal'a gelirinin yalnızca yüzde 25'ini harcamasını, kalan yüzde 75'ini ise biriktirmesini tavsiye etti. Gençliğinde savurganlığıyla dikkat çeken ve 20 yaşındayken tek bir günde 1 milyon dolar harcadığını daha önce açıklayan O'Neal, bu tavsiyenin ardından tasarrufa çok daha fazla önem vermeye başladığını söyledi. Servetini kaybetme ihtimaline karşı önlem aldı Basketboldan kazandığı milyonlarca doları farklı alanlarda değerlendiren O'Neal, bütün yatırımlarının başarılı olacağına güvenmek istemedi. Bu nedenle gelirinin önemli bir bölümünü, emeklilik döneminde kendisine düzenli ödeme yapılmasını sağlayacak finansal ürünlere aktardı. O'Neal, kararının arkasındaki düşünceyi, yatırımlarının başarısız olması veya beklenmedik gelişmeler yaşanması durumunda kendisine güvence oluşturmak istemesiyle açıkladı. ABD'de "annuity" olarak bilinen bu ürünler, sigorta şirketleri tarafından sunuluyor. Kişinin toplu para veya belirli dönemlerde prim ödemesi karşılığında gelecekte düzenli gelir elde etmesini sağlıyor. Ödemelerin tutarı ve süresi ise sözleşmenin koşullarına göre değişiyor. Ayda 1 milyon dolar gelir bekliyor Gelecek yılın bahar aylarında 55 yaşına girecek olan O'Neal, yıllar önce yaptığı bu yatırımların karşılığını almaya hazırlanıyor. Podcast sırasında emeklilik ürünlerinden ne kadar gelir beklediği sorulan eski basketbolcu, övünmek istemediğini ancak 55 yaşına geldiğinde aylık yaklaşık 1 milyon dolar alacağını düşündüğünü söyledi. Bu tutar, yılda yaklaşık 12 milyon dolarlık düzenli gelire karşılık geliyor. O'Neal, ödemelerin neredeyse hayatının geri kalanı boyunca devam etmesini beklediğini belirtti. Ancak ünlü basketbolcu, yatırdığı toplam tutara veya sözleşmelerinin ayrıntılarına ilişkin bilgi paylaşmadı. Çocuklarına servet için diploma şartı O'Neal, programda yalnızca yatırımlarını değil, çocuklarına yönelik servet yaklaşımını da anlattı. Çocuklarına sık sık "Biz zengin değiliz, ben zenginim" dediğini hatırlatan NBA efsanesi, aile servetinden yararlanabilmeleri için eğitimlerini tamamlamaları gerektiğini vurguladı. O'Neal, çocuklarından lisans ve yüksek lisans eğitimi almalarını beklediğini, aile parasına erişmek isteyenlerin iki veya üç diplomaya sahip olması gerektiğini söyledi. Kendisi de profesyonel basketbol kariyerine başladıktan sonra eğitimine devam eden O'Neal, lisans ve yüksek lisans derecelerinin yanı sıra eğitim alanında doktora derecesi aldı. Google yatırımından büyük kazanç sağladı O'Neal, podcast'te teknoloji devi Google'a yaptığı erken dönem yatırımı da yeniden gündeme getirdi. Bir otelin lobisinde tanıştığı kişinin kendisini henüz halka arz edilmemiş Google'a yatırım yapmaya davet ettiğini anlatan eski basketbolcu, finans danışmanıyla görüştükten sonra şirkete bir miktar para yatırdığını söyledi. Google'ın halka arzının ardından ilk yatırımcıların elde ettiği kazançları gazetelerden öğrendiğini belirten O'Neal, kendi yatırımından da önemli bir getiri sağladığını ifade etti. Ancak bu başarılı yatırımına rağmen 2009 yılındaki boşanmasında her şeyini kaybettiğini söyleyerek espri yaptı. O'Neal'ın anlattıkları, yüksek gelir elde etmenin yanında bu geliri korumaya yönelik uzun vadeli finansal planlamanın da servet yönetiminde önemli bir yer tuttuğunu ortaya koydu.

Ancak ünlü basketbolcu, yatırdığı toplam tutara veya sözleşmelerinin ayrıntılarına ilişkin bilgi paylaşmadı. Çocuklarına servet için diploma şartı O'Neal, programda yalnızca yatırımlarını değil, çocuklarına yönelik servet yaklaşımını da anlattı. Çocuklarına sık sık "Biz zengin değiliz, ben zenginim" dediğini hatırlatan NBA efsanesi, aile servetinden yararlanabilmeleri için eğitimlerini tamamlamaları gerektiğini vurguladı. O'Neal, çocuklarından lisans ve yüksek lisans eğitimi almalarını beklediğini, aile parasına erişmek isteyenlerin iki veya üç diplomaya sahip olması gerektiğini söyledi. Kendisi de profesyonel basketbol kariyerine başladıktan sonra eğitimine devam eden O'Neal, lisans ve yüksek lisans derecelerinin yanı sıra eğitim alanında doktora derecesi aldı. Google yatırımından büyük kazanç sağladı O'Neal, podcast'te teknoloji devi Google'a yaptığı erken dönem yatırımı da yeniden gündeme getirdi. Bir otelin lobisinde tanıştığı kişinin kendisini henüz halka arz edilmemiş Google'a yatırım yapmaya davet ettiğini anlatan eski basketbolcu, finans danışmanıyla görüştükten sonra şirkete bir miktar para yatırdığını söyledi. Google'ın halka arzının ardından ilk yatırımcıların elde ettiği kazançları gazetelerden öğrendiğini belirten O'Neal, kendi yatırımından da önemli bir getiri sağladığını ifade etti. Ancak bu başarılı yatırımına rağmen 2009 yılındaki boşanmasında her şeyini kaybettiğini söyleyerek espri yaptı. O'Neal'ın anlattıkları, yüksek gelir elde etmenin yanında bu geliri korumaya yönelik uzun vadeli finansal planlamanın da servet yönetiminde önemli bir yer tuttuğunu ortaya koydu.

items.titleTr: Altında faiz baskısına rağmen yükseliş umudu: Kritik tahmin açıklandı
items.summaryTr: Altın fiyatları, yükselen tahvil faizlerinin baskısı altında dalgalanırken UniCredit, 2026 yıl sonu tahmin aralığını 3 bin 900-4 bin 500 dolar seviyesinde tuttu.
items.articleText: Altında faiz baskısına rağmen yükseliş umudu: Kritik tahmin açıklandı Altın fiyatları, yükselen tahvil faizlerinin baskısı altında dalgalanırken UniCredit, 2026 yıl sonu tahmin aralığını 3 bin 900-4 bin 500 dolar seviyesinde tuttu. Altın fiyatları, haftanın son işlem gününde perşembe günkü yükselişin ardından yeniden geriledi. Ons altın, saat 16.50 GMT itibarıyla yüzde 0,54 düşüşle 4 bin 63,42 dolara indi. Buna karşın değerli metal, çarşamba günü 4 bin doların üzerine taşıdığı kazanımların büyük bölümünü korudu. UniCredit, kasım ayı değerlendirmesinde altın fiyatlarında kısa vadede dalgalı ve yatay bir seyrin devam edebileceğini belirtti. Banka, 2026 yıl sonu için ons altın tahmin aralığını 3 bin 900-4 bin 500 dolar olarak korudu. Bu aralığın, altının yıl sonuna kadar mutlaka 4 bin 500 dolara ulaşacağı anlamına gelmediği vurgulandı. Yükselen faizler altın üzerinde baskı oluşturuyor UniCredit'e göre, ABD Merkez Bankası'nın (Fed) daha uzun süre yüksek faiz politikasını sürdüreceği beklentisi ve yüksek reel faizler, altın fiyatlarının yükselişini sınırlayan temel unsurlar arasında yer alıyor. Ancak banka, tahvil faizlerindeki yükselişin nedeninin de önemli olduğuna dikkat çekti. Ekonomik büyümenin güçlenmesiyle artan faizlerin altın üzerinde baskı oluşturabileceği belirtilirken, bütçe açıkları ve kamu borcuna ilişkin endişeler nedeniyle yükselen faizlerin altını destekleyebileceği ifade edildi. Uzun vadeli tahvillerde yatırımcıların talep ettiği ek getiriyi ifade eden vade priminin, kamu maliyesine ilişkin risklerle yükselmesi durumunda yatırımcıların devlet tahvilleri dışındaki alternatif varlıklara yönelebileceği değerlendiriliyor. Altın fonlarında varlıklar rekor kırdı Altın fiyatlarındaki geri çekilmeye rağmen yatırımcı talebinde güçlü görünüm dikkat çekti. Dünya Altın Konseyi'nin ekim ayı raporuna göre, fiziki altın destekli borsa yatırım fonlarına (ETF) ekim ayında 2,7 milyar dolarlık giriş gerçekleşti. Bu girişlerle altın ETF'lerinin toplam varlığı ay sonunda 4 bin 275 tona ulaşarak rekor kırdı. Avrupa fonları girişlerde başı çekerken Asya'daki yatırımcılar da net alıcı konumunda kaldı. Kuzey Amerika fonlarında ise sınırlı çıkış görüldü. UniCredit, merkez bankalarının güçlü altın alımlarının, fonlardaki rekor varlıkların ve yatırımcıların portföylerini çeşitlendirme eğiliminin fiyatlardaki olası düşüşü sınırlayabileceğini belirtti. Borsalardaki düşüş altının güvenli liman rolünü yeniden gündeme getirdi Perşembe günü hisse senedi piyasalarında yaşanan satış dalgası sırasında altının performansı da dikkat çekti. JPMorgan'ın işlem masası değerlendirmesinde, altının S&P 500 endeksine kıyasla yaklaşık yüzde 5 daha iyi performans gösterdiği belirtildi. Bu gelişme, altının piyasalardaki belirsizlik dönemlerinde güvenli liman özelliğini yeniden öne çıkardı. Ancak tek günlük performansın, altının hisse senedi piyasalarındaki her düşüşte benzer bir koruma sağlayacağını göstermediği de değerlendiriliyor. UniCredit'ten altın fiyatları için kademeli toparlanma beklentisi UniCredit, yüksek faizlerin kısa vadede altının yükselişini sınırlayabileceğini, ancak yapısal talep ve kamu borcuna ilişkin risklerin fiyatlardaki aşağı yönlü hareketi frenleyebileceğini öngörüyor. Banka, bu unsurların etkisiyle altın fiyatlarında zaman içinde kademeli bir toparlanma yaşanabileceği görüşünü koruyor. Altın, faiz getirisi sunmayan bir yatırım aracı olduğu için reel faizlerin yükseldiği dönemlerde genellikle baskı altında kalıyor. Buna karşılık jeopolitik belirsizlikler, kamu borcuna ilişkin endişeler, merkez bankalarının altın alımları ve ETF girişleri değerli metale olan talebi artırabiliyor. Bu sebepten tahvil faizleri ile altın fiyatları arasındaki ilişki, faizlerin hangi ekonomik ve mali gelişmeler nedeniyle yükseldiğine bağlı olarak değişebiliyor.

items.title: Turistik Doğu Ekspresi için bilet fiyatları belli oldu
items.summary: Ankara-Kars hattında 21 Aralık’ta yeniden seferlerine başlayacak Turistik Doğu Ekspresi’nde iki kişilik kompartıman fiyatları Aralık ayında 15 bin TL’den başlayacak, sömestr tatilinde 20 bin TL’ye çıkacak.
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: Turistik Doğu Ekspresi için bilet fiyatları belli oldu
items.summaryTr: Ankara-Kars hattında 21 Aralık’ta yeniden seferlerine başlayacak Turistik Doğu Ekspresi’nde iki kişilik kompartıman fiyatları Aralık ayında 15 bin TL’den başlayacak, sömestr tatilinde 20 bin TL’ye çıkacak.
items.articleText: Turistik Doğu Ekspresi için bilet fiyatları belli oldu - Ankara-Kars hattında 21 Aralık’ta yeniden seferlerine başlayacak Turistik Doğu Ekspresi’nde iki kişilik kompartıman fiyatları Aralık ayında 15 bin TL’den başlayacak, sömestr tatilinde 20 bin TL’ye çıkacak. Kış turizminin gözde rotalarından Turistik Doğu Ekspresi, 2026-2027 sezonunda yeniden yolcularını ağırlamaya hazırlanıyor. Turistik Doğu Ekspresi ne zaman seferlere başlayacak? CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Ankara ile Kars arasında düzenlenecek seferlerin ilk hareket tarihi 21 Aralık olarak açıklandı. Tren, Ankara’dan Kars’a ilk yolculuğunu bu tarihte gerçekleştirecek. Dönüş seferi ise 23 Aralık’ta Kars’tan Ankara’ya yapılacak. Kars Turizm Birliği Başkanı Halit Özer, yeni sezon öncesinde sefer takvimi ve bilet fiyatlarına ilişkin bilgi verdi. Özer, Turistik Doğu Ekspresi'nin normal Doğu Ekspresi ile karıştırılmaması gerektiğini belirterek iki trenin güzergâh ve seyahat özelliklerinin farklı olduğunu vurguladı. İki kişilik kompartıman fiyatları ne kadar? Turistik Doğu Ekspresi’nde bilet fiyatları seyahat dönemine göre farklılık gösteriyor. İki kişinin konaklayabildiği kompartımanların fiyatı Aralık ayında 15 bin TL olarak belirlendi. Ocak ayının sonlarına doğru fiyat 18 bin TL'ye yükselirken, sömestr tatilinde iki kişilik kompartıman için 20 bin TL ödenecek. Biletlerin yüzde 40'ı doğrudan satılacak TCDD Taşımacılık A.Ş., Turistik Doğu Ekspresi biletlerinin yüzde 60'ını TÜRSAB onaylı seyahat acenteleri üzerinden satışa sunacak. Kalan yüzde 40'lık bölüm ise doğrudan vatandaşlara ayrılacak. Doğrudan satışa sunulan biletler TCDD'nin mobil uygulaması üzerinden alınabilecek. Acentelere ayrılan kontenjan için ise ilgili seyahat şirketlerine başvurulabilecek. Kars Turizm Birliği Başkanı Halit Özer, kış manzaraları eşliğinde nostaljik bir yolculuk deneyimi sunan tren için yerli ve yabancı turistleri Kars'a davet etti.

items.title: Footage shows derailed carriages after fatal train crash in Egypt
items.summary: At least seven people died when two trains collided, causing several carriages to derail and fall down an embankment.

items.titleTr: Footage shows derailed carriages after fatal train crash in Egypt
items.summaryTr: At least seven people died when two trains collided, causing several carriages to derail and fall down an embankment.
items.articleText: Footage shows derailed carriages after fatal train crash in Egypt A train collision has killed at least seven people and injured dozens in northern Egypt. Footage showed multiple overturned carriages and dozens of people surrounding them. One train was travelling from Giza to the Fayoum oasis, south west of Cairo, while the other was heading from Cairo to Aswan in the south. It is yet unclear what caused the accident but Egyptian President Abdul Fattah al-Sisi said an investigation was underway and would "hold accountable anyone who proves their negligence".

items.title: Apple'ın patronu Türkiye'de: Tim Cook'tan Türkçe mesaj
items.summary: Apple'ın patronu Türkiye'de: Tim Cook'tan Türkçe mesaj
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: Apple'ın patronu Türkiye'de: Tim Cook'tan Türkçe mesaj
items.summaryTr: Apple'ın patronu Türkiye'de: Tim Cook'tan Türkçe mesaj
items.articleText: Apple'ın patronu Türkiye'de: Tim Cook'tan Türkçe mesaj YAYIN TARİHİ, 08 Kasım 2026 18:58 GÜNCELLEME, 08 Kasım 2026 19:26 PAYLAŞ - Apple'ın eski CEO'su ve mevcut Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı Tim Cook, sürpriz bir ziyaret için İstanbul'a geldi. Kapalıçarşı'dan "Merhaba Istanbul!" mesajı paylaşan Cook'un Türkiye ziyaretinin nedeni ortaya çıktı. ABD'li teknoloji devi Apple'ın yöneticisi Tim Cook, İstanbul ziyareti kapsamında tarihi Kapalıçarşı'yı gezdi. Cook, içerik üreticisi Cem Başak ile birlikte gerçekleştirdiği ziyaretten bir görüntüyü sosyal medya hesabında paylaştı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Paylaşımına Türkçe "Merhaba İstanbul!" sözleriyle başlayan Cook, Kapalıçarşı'nın manzarasından etkilendiğini belirtti. Cook, mesajında şu ifadelere yer verdi: "Merhaba İstanbul! Bu sabah yetenekli içerik üreticisi Cem Başak ile birlikte Kapalıçarşı'dan ne kadar muhteşem bir manzara! Bu olağanüstü ülkeyi ziyaret etmekten büyük heyecan duyuyorum!" Cook'un İstanbul ziyaretinin programına ve Türkiye'de gerçekleştireceği diğer temaslara ilişkin ise henüz bir açıklama yapılmadı. Kaynak: cnbce.com

CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Paylaşımına Türkçe "Merhaba İstanbul!" sözleriyle başlayan Cook, Kapalıçarşı'nın manzarasından etkilendiğini belirtti. Cook, mesajında şu ifadelere yer verdi: "Merhaba İstanbul! Bu sabah yetenekli içerik üreticisi Cem Başak ile birlikte Kapalıçarşı'dan ne kadar muhteşem bir manzara! Bu olağanüstü ülkeyi ziyaret etmekten büyük heyecan duyuyorum!" Cook'un İstanbul ziyaretinin programına ve Türkiye'de gerçekleştireceği diğer temaslara ilişkin ise henüz bir açıklama yapılmadı. items.title: Government 'looking seriously' at banning under-16s from Vinted and eBay
items.summary: The culture secretary confirms reports they could be in the list of platforms set to be banned next March.

items.titleTr: Government 'looking seriously' at banning under-16s from Vinted and eBay
items.summaryTr: The culture secretary confirms reports they could be in the list of platforms set to be banned next March.
items.articleText: Government 'looking seriously' at banning under-16s from Vinted and eBay - Published Vinted and eBay could be included in the list of platforms set to be banned for children aged under 16, the culture secretary has said. Lisa Nandy said the government was "looking seriously" at including the retailing websites in the social media ban "to keep children safe". The UK's social media ban for under-16s is set to come into force in March next year, with children barred from accessing platforms such as Instagram, TikTok and Snapchat. In response, eBay said it was looking forward to "understanding more and continuing to work constructively with the government". Vinted said it welcomed "open dialogue" with ministers and the regulator on the issue. Asked on the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg programme whether the government was looking to ban under-16s from Vinted and eBay, Nandy said: "We are looking seriously at doing so in order to keep children safe." It came after the Sunday Times reported, external that the UK's social media ban was being expanded to include the popular second-hand online marketplaces. The move was due to fears that messaging functions on the platforms allowed strangers to groom children, according to the newspaper. It suggested similar reselling platforms, Depop and Facebook Marketplace, would also be included in the list of banned sites. Businesses and individuals sell a host of goods on eBay, which has been a major global player in the online reselling market for years. The platform states on its website that it currently requires all of its members to be over 18 years old because listings involve "entering into a contract". Vinted is aimed at over 18s, but its terms and conditions do allow parents or guardians to create accounts for their children, which must be used under parental supervision. The site, on which users mostly buy and sell unwanted clothes and other fashion items, has grown rapidly recently to reach 17 million UK users. A Vinted spokesperson said direct messaging was "part of how the platform works" but that it had a "zero tolerance for harmful or explicit content" and had moderation teams and tools to spot and remove "activity that breaks our rules". "When we identify inappropriate behaviour, we take action, up to a permanent ban or reporting to the relevant authorities," they said. An eBay spokesperson said the company was "focused on providing a trusted and safe marketplace experience for our millions of customers". "While the details of the proposed legislation are not yet clear, we look forward to understanding more and continuing to work constructively with the government," they added. The government announced it would ban under-16s accessing social media in June this year, with children prevented from accessing 10 of the biggest platforms. YouTube will also be banned for under-16s, but YouTube Kids - a version of the video-sharing app designed to be safe for children - will not be included in the measures. A complete list of affected platforms has not yet been released, but the government said it would cover those "whose purpose is to enable social interaction and which allow users to post material". That means platforms that have livestreaming or features that enable the potential for strangers to contact children will also be restricted, which includes gaming sites. It does not mean that Roblox, the biggest gaming site in the UK for those aged eight to 12, for example, will be banned for under-16s. However, certain features such as its chat function will be restricted. But Matthew Sinclair, a senior director at the Computer and Communications Industry Association, which represents tech companies, argued that ministers should prevent the rules having "scope creep". He said a restriction on messaging for under-16s "would not stop at social media and would reach into the services families depend on to stay in touch", and urged the government to "ensure any new restrictions are proportionate and effective." The UK's ban comes after a similar one was introduced in Australia last year. Many children there have found ways to get round it, but the UK has said it intends to take a tougher approach. In recent weeks, attention has turned to how a social media ban would be enforced. Last month, the communications regulator Ofcom set out its recommendations for the most effective ways to identify which of the UK's millions of social media users are aged over 16. Rani Govender, head of online child safety at the NSPCC, said the "real question" going forward was how the government ensured age checks were effective. "But effective age checks are only part of the solution," she added. "Tech companies must also be required to build child safety into every platform, device and AI tool, so children are protected from harmful and illegal content and only able to access age-appropriate services." items.title: Iran executes three men for 'armed unrest' after January protests
items.summary: It is claimed Hassan Dioband, Hamid Kazemi and Reza Zanganeh were part of anti-government protests earlier this year.
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: Iran executes three men for 'armed unrest' after January protests
items.summaryTr: It is claimed Hassan Dioband, Hamid Kazemi and Reza Zanganeh were part of anti-government protests earlier this year.
items.articleText: Iran executes three men for 'armed unrest' after January protests - Published Iran has executed three men accused of carrying out armed unrest during January's anti-government protests, according to state media. Hassan Dioband, Hamid Kazemi and Reza Zanganeh were accused of throwing Molotov cocktails and grenades, using bladed weapons and firearms, and setting fire to public facilities in the city of Karaj, west of Tehran, Iran's state news agency Tasnim, external reported. The executions are the latest in a series linked to the protests, including those of people accused of having ties to Israel and the United States. The number of executions in Iran has increased since US-Israeli strikes on the Islamic Republic began in late February. The protest movement initially sparked in December last year by the high cost of living rapidly evolved into widespread anti-government demonstrations that peaked on 8 and 9 of January. Iranian authorities reported more than 3,000 deaths, and blamed the violence on "terrorist acts" orchestrated by the US and Israel. However foreign-based NGOs gave higher figures and the BBC received multiple accounts from Iranians of security forces opening fire on unarmed protesters. Tasnim reported that the three men were executed after the Supreme Court upheld their convictions and found them guilty of "participating in operational activities on behalf of the Israeli Zionist regime, the United States and hostile groups". The damage allegedly included an electricity substation in Karaj which caused power outages in some areas. Dioband was arrested on 11 January after investigations identified him as a suspect in attacks on public property and incitement to violence. Ten others accused of taking part in the unrest under his supervision were later arrested. Reuters news agency reports that they received prison terms of 5 to 10 years. The latest executions in Iran come after the UN human rights chief Volker Türk said he was alarmed by the rise in death penalties. In August, Türk said at least 56 people had been executed on national security-related charges since 19 March, including 27 in cases linked to January's nationwide anti-government protests. Iran is thought to be the world's second-most prolific executioner after China. Last year, it put to death at least 2,159 people, according to Amnesty International. The human rights group said that was the highest figure on record since 1981 and included 45 executions of suspected dissidents on national security-related charges. items.titleTr: Here’s what happened in crypto today
items.summaryTr: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
items.articleText: Here’s what happened in crypto today Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation. Today in crypto: Binance France is closing up shop in the country, as all accounts will be closed on Dec. 31. The US Treasury imposed financial sanctions on eight Canadian money-service companies it claims have done business with sanctioned Iranian entities, and the Treasury also moved to cut MEXC off from the US financial system over alleged illicit transactions. Binance France emails announce closure of accounts Dec. 31 Binance France is closing up shop in the country. Customers have been notified by email during early November, according to media reports. All accounts will be closed on Dec. 31, and any assets left on the exchange will be charged monthly fees starting on Nov. 29, Cryptoast, Crypto Briefing and other media reported on Saturday, citing emails sent to users by Binance. On that date, accounts still maintaining a balance will pay a monthly maintenance fee of 0.025% of the balance, or a minimum of 10 USDC, a stablecoin tracking the US dollar. To avoid fees, withdrawals must be completed by Nov. 29, the exchange said. US sanctions Canadian money-exchange firms over Iran ties The US Treasury imposed financial sanctions on eight Canadian money-service companies it claims have done business with sanctioned Iranian entities. These companies facilitated the exchange of Iranian rials and other currencies for digital assets, enabling international transactions, a US Treasury Department statement said on Friday. The sanctions, which serve to isolate the companies from the dollar-based financial system, are the latest in a series of Treasury moves against firms outside the US. These businesses have facilitated transactions with sanctioned Iranian digital asset exchanges, as well as with digital asset addresses associated with Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), according to the Treasury. US Treasury cuts off MEXC over alleged $16B in illicit transactions The US Department of Treasury on Friday issued an order to cut cryptocurrency exchange MEXC Global off from the US’ financial system after accusing it of facilitating at least $16 billion in transactions linked to sanctions evasion, cybercrime and other illicit activity. The Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) asserted that MEXC handled transactions involving sanctioned groups in Iran, Russia and North Korea between May 2021 and May 2026. This included around $1.5 billion in transactions linked to Russian sanctions evasion, according to the official press release. The order effectively bans US financial institutions from processing money transfers involving MEXC and will take effect 30 days after it is published in the Federal Register. “Financial institutions cannot have it both ways: Either you support the Iranian regime, or you have access to the U.S. financial system,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent. “Treasury will continue to sever the Iranian regime’s economic lifelines and thwart its desperate attempts to circumvent U.S. sanctions using digital assets.” The action is part of Operation Economic Outcast, a US Treasury campaign launched in August with aims to cut off financial entities that help Iran evade sanctions. According to DefiLlama, the exchange held about $4.48 billion in total assets as of Friday. Cointelegraph contacted MEXC for comment but had not received a response by publication.

On that date, accounts still maintaining a balance will pay a monthly maintenance fee of 0.025% of the balance, or a minimum of 10 USDC, a stablecoin tracking the US dollar. To avoid fees, withdrawals must be completed by Nov. 29, the exchange said. A Binance email cited by Cryptoast said: “Due to the orderly cessation of activities, your Binance France account will close as of December 31, 2026. If you have not withdrawn your crypto-assets as of December 31, 2026, this message constitutes a notification of our intention to consider your account inactive, in accordance with our Terms of Use. This can result in the conversion, transfer or other processing of your crypto-assets.” Key services restricted in June Related: Binance’s EU services face scrutiny over licensing exemption: Report Cointelegraph reported in late June that Binance had notified European Union users access to key services would be restricted after the exchange failed to secure Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) regulatory authorization from a member state before a July 1 deadline. According to media reports, Binance’s global client base counts at least 300 million customers, while the app was downloaded more than 4 million times in the EU last year. items.articleText: Amsterdam protesters break into Microsoft data center construction site: Report Dutch police said they detained 150-200 people for trespassing during the protest. Protesters reportedly broke into an Amsterdam construction site for a Microsoft data center and clashed with police. Dutch authorities said they detained 150-200 people for trespassing. One protester told a local broadcaster they were trying to stop construction of the data center, according to a report from the Associated Press on Friday. The report added that Microsoft was aware of the demonstration and responded through a spokesperson: “We understand that people feel strongly about the project, and we respect their right to express those views peacefully,” they said. “However, we do not condone any actions that are unlawful or that put people’s safety at risk.” A tougher regulatory environment in the US is expected to follow the recent midterm elections, which saw a wave of Democrats promising to clamp down on data centers, which use large amounts of electricity and water, AP reported. Cointelegraph reported in September that the town of Plattsburgh, New York, held a public hearing to discuss a temporary land use moratorium for operations including AI data centers and crypto mining. items.titleTr: How the deadly shooting in Krakow unfolded
items.summaryTr: Video authenticated by BBC Verify shows the moment gunshots rang out in Krakow's main market square.
items.articleText: How the deadly shooting in Krakow unfolded Six people were killed and several others injured when a gunman opened fire in central Krakow, Poland's second largest city, on Saturday. Footage authenticated by BBC Verify shows about a dozen people running inside two buildings before a black car with its front window open passes, followed by a police car. Another video shows the moment that gunshots were heard in the city's main market square. items.articleText: Binance’s finance chief Kaiser Ng to leave company, report says Ng will be replaced by Justin Yek, who was formerly vice-president of finance at Airwallex. Binance’s finance chief Kaiser Ng is reportedly leaving that company to pursue a new venture. “Kaiser Ng has decided to pursue a new venture after more than five years at Binance, with a transition plan implemented over the last half year,” Binance co-CEO Yi He said in a statement obtained by Reuters on Saturday. Ng’s LinkedIn profile says he has been Binance’s chief financial officer since January 2022 and before that served in the same capacity at crypto exchange Kraken for about five years. He will be replaced by Justin Yek, who was formerly vice-president of finance at Airwallex, according to the report. The news comes a little more than a week after Binance was hacked for a record $6.3 billion. Cointelegraph reported that hackers stole about $6.3 billion from Binance on Oct. 29, in the largest cryptocurrency theft on record. Binance said it would absorb the losses rather than pass them on to customers. The attack has been attributed to North Korean hackers by the FBI and several researchers, a charge that country has denied. Magazine: Asian crypto exchanges batten down the hatches as hacks surge: Asia Express

items.titleTr: Traders 'priced out' of £12,000 Christmas market pitches
items.summaryTr: Stall holders said they'd met the council leader to express their concerns at high costs since a new operator took over.
items.articleText: Traders 'priced out' of £12,000 Christmas market pitches - Published Traders claim they have been priced out of this year's Christmas market. They have told Liverpool City Council leader Liam Robinson that they cannot afford to take space at the event now that a new operator has taken over running it. Anthony Grice said he had been quoted £12,000 to take a stall at the St George's Plateau attraction. Robinson said he had met business owners to "understand the challenges and the issues that they might have had this year" so the authority could look at different options in future. He said the council had been aware of the price structure being offered to traders by the new operator, Underbelly, when it won the contract to run the event. And he added that the council would get a share of some of the income. But Grice said it felt like local traders' concerns were being "swept under the carpet" during a meeting to discuss the plans. He said: "I asked how many local traders had signed up, and the council didn't know". He added: "These markets should be a chance to showcase the best of what you've got, but not having the 'Scouse soul' there is so annoying. "Aren't our people good enough?" Jeweller Alex Healy, from Gateacre, rang a BBC Radio Merseyside phone-in to tell Robinson that she would not be returning to the market this year, despite having been a trader at previous markets since 2021. She said "It would cost me in the region of £14,000 to £15,000. I have the smallest hut available, but that price I physically cannot afford it." She said she was acutely aware of the cost-of-living crisis facing her customers, adding: "I don't want to raise my prices. I shouldn't have to." Robinson said he wanted entrepreneurs like Healy to succeed and invited her to meet him to look at ways the council could support her business. He added Underbelly had won the tender to run the market "on quality and price" and had a "track record of delivering these markets successfully in lots of other places across the country". Underbelly has been contacted for comment. The leader of the Liberal Democrat opposition group on the council, Carl Cashman, said £14,000 was "a rip-off". He added: "Small businesses are feeling the pinch at the moment, with rising business rates, inflation, and payroll costs, and consumers spending less. "So £14,000 is just a risk too big for them to take, and the market won't be as good for it." A Liverpool city council spokesperson said local traders would be able to sell artisan goods at a street market on Basnett Street running on each Saturday in November, plus at regular and pop-up markets in Lark Lane and Woolton Village in the run-up to Christmas. items.summary: Saudi Arabia, which leads a coalition fighting the Houthis in Yemen, has not commented.

items.titleTr: Houthis say at least 33 killed in Saudi air strike
items.summaryTr: Saudi Arabia, which leads a coalition fighting the Houthis in Yemen, has not commented.
items.articleText: Houthis say at least 33 killed in Saudi air strike - Published Media linked to the Houthi movement in Yemen say at least 33 people, including women and children, have been killed in air strikes by Saudi Arabia. There has been no comment from the Saudi-led coalition backing the internationally recognised government in Yemen. Live video footage on Al Masirah - a television station run by the Houthis - has shown rescuers pulling bodies out of the rubble of several buildings in al-Shariyah, a town to the east of the capital, Sanaa. The bodies of young children can be seen among those dug out from the ruins. The television station has also shown a number of injured people being carried on stretchers to hospital. Saba news agency, which is also run by the Houthis, said the attack was carried out by Saudi Arabia on Saturday. It added that 39 people had been injured. The Saudis have led a coalition that has been fighting the Houthis for more than a decade in support of Yemen's internationally recognised government. The war in Yemen had been dormant for several years but reignited as a result of the Iran war. A truce began to fall apart when Saudi Arabia struck the airport in Sanaa - which is controlled by the Houthis - to prevent an Iranian plane landing there. The Tehran-backed Houthis subsequently targeted Abha airport in Saudi Arabia, then began hitting Saudi ships that have been using the Red Sea off the coast of Yemen as an alternative oil export route to the Strait of Hormuz. Major fighting has since resumed in Yemen between the Houthis and forces fighting for the Saudi-backed government of Yemen. On Friday, an attack on a market in Taiz province, which has been the focus of much of the recent fighting, is reported to have killed 30 people. The Houthis accused the Saudis of carrying out the strike, while government forces accused the Houthis of having fired a missile at the site. The United Nations says more than 1,600 people have been killed and more than 300,000 displaced since fighting resumed. The Saudis have regularly bombed Houthi positions, while the group has fired multiple missiles at targets inside Saudi Arabia, including airports and oil facilities. Hours before the strike that hit al-Shariyah, the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted a missile heading towards Riyadh. The Saudi Ministry of Energy later said the Aramco tower had been hit by falling shrapnel in what it said was an attempted attack. The state-owned oil company's building suffered minor damage. A Houthi leader, Mahdi al-Mashat, has vowed that the group will take revenge for the latest attacks in Yemen.

items.title: The Trump coalition is shattered - what will Republicans do now?
items.summary: Republicans can stick with Trumpism or chart a new path, writes BBC Washington correspondent Daniel Bush.

items.titleTr: The Trump coalition is shattered - what will Republicans do now?
items.summaryTr: Republicans can stick with Trumpism or chart a new path, writes BBC Washington correspondent Daniel Bush.
items.articleText: The Trump coalition is shattered - what will Republicans do now? - Published Republicans are in soul-searching mode after the coalition that powered Donald Trump to three straight presidential nominations imploded in spectacular fashion in the 2026 midterms. The stunning election defeat immediately raised questions about the party's future post-Trump. But there are no easy answers as Republicans face the choice of doubling down on Trumpism or trying to chart a new path forward in his final years in office. The depth of the problem was captured by outgoing Florida Governor Ron DeSantis, who called the midterms "close to an extinction-level event for Republicans". Others struck a more optimistic tone. Vice-President JD Vance, who blamed the midterm results on public anger over the war with Iran, argued the party could turn things around. Nevertheless Vance acknowledged the fallout will be messy. "There will be a lot of infighting and arguing over what happened and why," Vance said. The wide range of reactions on the right highlights deep fault lines in the party that formed around Trump's improbable rise to the presidency in 2016 and never really went away. It's too early to tell which faction will win. But while Republicans are still licking their wounds, the intraparty battle Vance predicted is already under way. The party must decide whether it will be "centred on one figure, one guy, or on a wider set of ideas like conservatism that can win outside the deepest red places," Rina Shah, a Republican strategist, told the BBC. Critics on the right - the "Never Trumpers" who opposed his first White House campaign - are pushing for a return to the Republican Party's pre-Trump roots, citing the historic losses around the country on election night. But simply turning back the clock on Trump will be extremely difficult if not impossible to do. The party has been wholly transformed during Trump's decade-long reign. Most Republicans have shifted to the right on domestic issues like immigration, and rejected the interventionist foreign policy of the George W Bush era that led to the wars in Iraq and Afghanistan. In Congress, the more moderate establishment wing of the party that disliked Trump from the start has almost entirely disappeared, replaced by conservative Trump backers who echo his nativism and populist rhetoric. That trend continued this year, as old-guard Republicans like John Cornyn in Texas and Maine's Susan Collins, both of whom clashed with Trump over the years, were voted out of office. Three days after the election Trump appointed Stephen Miller as his new White House chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles. The move signalled Trump has no plans to moderate his policies or message in his remaining years in office. Miller, who had been serving as the president's chief domestic policy adviser, is a longtime Trump aide known for his hardline immigration policies. - With Stephen Miller pick, Trump readies for a battle - Published1 day ago - How America voted in maps and charts - Published2 days ago One of the architects of the Make America Great Again (Maga) movement, Steve Bannon, predicted a "civil war" in the party after the midterms. Afterwards, he blamed the Republicans' defeat on the economy and "foreign wars". "I don't think we implemented the Maga programme," he said, calling on Trump to double down on mass deportations. But other Republican strategists said the midterms were a wake up call for Make America Great Again (Maga) loyalists who want Trump's political movement to outlast his presidency. "There's still plenty of Maga voters out there who have supported Donald Trump through thick and thin," said Whit Ayres, a Republican strategist. "But there is also a significant portion of the Republican Party that's non-Maga, and that's a majority now." Should Republican hopefuls distance themselves from Trump? The party lost control of the House and Senate, as well as governorships and state legislatures in red states like Texas and Kansas where Democrats had been shut out of power for decades - and where Trump won by double digits when he was on the ballot. The stunning upsets underscored the fickle nature of political coalitions. Trump expanded the Republican base in 2024, increasing support with Latinos and younger voters among other key groups. Republicans hailed the gains as a sign of future strength for the party. Just two years later, the party lost ground with nearly every critical voting bloc. According to a New York Times analysis of voter data, Latino support for Democratic candidates increased by 29 percentage points from 2024-26. Support from young voters 18-29 years old increased by 33 points. The swings reflected polling ahead of the midterms that found widespread disapproval with Trump's handling of the economy, immigration and the war with Iran. Democrats also capitalised on a public perception that the Trump family and administration is rife with self-dealing and corruption. The president's focus on the White House ballroom and other Washington construction projects also contributed to a sense among voters that he was more focused on his legacy than addressing affordability issues. It's a sentiment shared by Benjamin Shrader, the leader of the Young Republicans in Austin, who was still shell-shocked when he spoke to the BBC in Texas the morning after his party was almost wiped out in the state by a Democratic "blue tsunami". Shrader said Trump was still a "force of nature" when asked to reflect on how the president had used his first public appearance after the results to show off the White House ballroom project. He hesitated before adding: "I would focus on issues that are not ballrooms, that are not renaming things. I would focus on what matters." The evidence in the immediate aftermath of the midterms suggests that Republicans could benefit by distancing themselves from Trump ahead of 2028. 'Vance was the favourite - now the race is wide open' Vance tried to thread the needle with his midterm assessment blaming the Iran war and calling for a return to "America First." It was a nuanced critique that broke with Trump on an unpopular war, but embraced a broader political brand that remains popular with the Maga base. Trump's next moves on Iran will be watched closely by the party for their 2028 implications. An escalation would risk fuelling the concerns voiced by Vance and other "America First" proponents. In his postmortem statement on X, Vance also echoed the growing calls on the right to reexamine US support for Israel. But he also signalled an openness to making some immigration enforcement changes. That clashes with Miller, a Vance ally who has speared the administration's second-term immigration agenda. Party strategists said the midterm drubbing complicated Vance's path to the nomination. "Before this midterm, JD Vance was the odds-on favourite to win the Republican nomination in 2028. After this midterm, the nomination battle is completely wide open," Ayres said. Potential Trump successors have some time to consider their options, but they'll have to make up their minds relatively soon. Any 2028 presidential hopefuls will face pressure to announce White House bids in the next few months. Some could launch campaigns before the end of the year. Vance's election analysis was widely interpreted as an unofficial signal of his plans to run. It will likely be a crowded primary field. Other rumoured White House contenders include Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Senator Ted Cruz of Texas, Florida Governor DeSantis, former US ambassador to the United Nations Nikki Haley and former New Jersey Governor Chris Christie, to name a few. In the next election cycle, Republican presidential and congressional candidates alike will have tough decisions to make on key issues of the day, from US support for Israel to tariffs to the AI boom. Trump's power may be diminished as he enters the final two years of his second term, but he'll still have the loudest voice in the party over the next two years. It's unclear whether he will get deeply involved in the process or take a hands-off approach. Trump has praised Vance and Rubio at different times, but typically deflects questions about who he'd like to see succeed him. His endorsement will loom as the biggest wildcard in the 2028 Republican primary race. "It remains to be seen who will jump into that race," Ayres said. "But I think it's going to be a lot larger and more diverse than we anticipated before the midterm election." Follow the twists and turns of Trump's second term with North America correspondent Anthony Zurcher's US Politics Unspun newsletter. Readers in the UK can sign up here. Those outside the UK can sign up here. - Published1 day ago

items.articleText: Germans wrestle with what to do with Hitler's destroyed Eagle's Nest retreat - Published Perched on a ridge high up in the spectacular scenery of the German Alps lie the burned-out ruins of a mountain house called The Eagle's Nest, which is now at the heart of an intense debate about Germany's Nazi past. Known in German as Kehlsteinhaus, the retreat was built by the Nazis in 1938, and frequented by Adolf Hitler and other high-ranking Nazis and their guests. After World War Two it was classified as a historical monument recalling the Nazi era. Last month it was gutted by fire in a suspected arson attack, and some believe it should be completely destroyed, the site returned to nature and all memory of its Nazi past forgotten. But others want it either partially or completely rebuilt, wary of the risk of turning it into a site for Neo-Nazi pilgrimage at a time when Germany is witnessing the resurgence of the far-right. Germany has an "everlasting responsibility to communicate, to deal with our Nazi past", said Isabel Heinemann, professor of contemporary history at Munich's Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität (LMU). But rebuilding the site completely, she warned, would mean putting "highly ideologised or highly ideological architecture" back in place. Before it was burned down during the evening of 23 October, the Eagle's Nest had been a popular tourist attraction, owned by the state of Bavaria and operating for many years as a restaurant. Visitors would take a bus and then ride the original brass and mirror-panelled lift through the mountain to the Kehlsteinhaus to savour the magnificent views above the town of Berchtesgaden. Once there, they could eat sausages in the beer garden on the Obersalzberg at 1,834m (6,017ft) above sea level, overlooking the Alps. Unlike Hitler's nearby summer residence, the Berghof, which was bombed in World War Two and demolished in 1952, the Eagle's Nest survived the war. Tens of thousands of tourists visited each season, providing an important source of income to the region. In the 1990s, amid concerns that the site did not do enough to confront the crimes of the Nazi past, a museum, the Obersalzberg Documentation Centre, was opened close by. Around 15 years ago, a photo exhibit was opened in the Kehlsteinhaus about its history. Although the Eagle's Nest itself was "largely destroyed" by the fire, according to police, the documentation centre survived unscathed. The authorities have not commented on a possible motive, but a 33-year-old man with a history of mental illness has been detained in a secure psychiatric hospital on suspicion of arson. - Man arrested after fire at Hitler's mountaintop Eagle's Nest retreat - Published24 October Some feel this is the moment to allow the site to fade into history. "It's been torched now. It's been destroyed. I think they should just clear away the rubble and leave the mountain as it should be in its natural state," said Prof Sir Richard J. Evans, a specialist in Nazi Germany at the University of Cambridge. That has happened with "quite a few other Nazi sites", he argued, including the bunker in Berlin where Hitler killed himself: "The bunker was filled in with concrete and a children's playground put on the top of it on the ground." The Kehlsteinhaus was just "a Nazi vanity project" since romanticised by the name Eagle's Nest, he said. But Bavaria's authorities take a different view about the site's future. Both the state's interior minister, Joachim Herrmann, and its minister for the arts, Markus Blume, have spoken out in favour of rebuilding the Kehlsteinhaus. "We can hardly leave a ruin standing there," Herrmann said. Sven Keller, head of the Obersalzberg Documentation Centre, believes it is important not to leave the site in ruins, as that could encourage Neo-Nazi pilgrims, who would be able to hike up there completely undisturbed. "We have quite some experience at Obersalzberg with what happens if we clear those sites. Hitler's Berghof was demolished in the 1950s, and in our experience, this does not remove such sites from the mental maps of people," he told the BBC's Today programme. Nor does he believe "a one-on-one reconstruction" of the site is possible, and Blume has made clear on Bavarian radio that "it should not and must not cost the taxpayer anything". Herrmann said they would look for a sensible solution in consultation with historians, given the historically complex circumstances surrounding the building. Heinemann, who also heads the Leibniz Institute for Contemporary History, believes full-scale reconstruction should be "out of the question". "I rather think we can document the state left by the fire and also document the historical remains of the Kehlsteinhaus, and then reconstruct parts in a modern design, to make clear the different layers of time that can be seen in this building," she told the BBC. Germany and Austria have long struggled to deal with the fraught legacy of buildings and sites connected to the Nazi era. With the recent rise of the far-right AfD and the Austrian Freedom Party, the debate over Erinnerungskultur (Culture of Remembrance) has taken on a new urgency. A row broke out recently in Germany when AfD and conservative CDU councillors in a town in Saxony decided to ban "stumbling stones" memorials - embedded small brass plaques in the streets - to victims of the Nazis. In Austria over the summer, a police station was opened in the house where Hitler was born in Braunau am Inn. It followed years of controversy about how the house should be used. The Austrian government said the police presence would help prevent neo-Nazi pilgrims. But others had wanted the house to become a centre of responsibility, actively confronting the Nazi past. As one resident of Braunau am Inn told me, it was a delicate balance between how much to remember and how much to forget. Related topics - Published26 September

items.summaryTr: Yaroch paid off his debts and intended to use the proceeds to finance a new life in Portugal, where he planned to buy a vineyard.
items.articleText: Ex-FBI counterintelligence agent stole almost $2.5M in crypto Yaroch paid off his debts and intended to use the proceeds to finance a new life in Portugal, where he planned to buy a vineyard. A former FBI counterintelligence agent admitted to wire fraud and money laundering in stealing almost $2.5 million in cryptocurrency from unidentified adversarial nations and wallets that were under investigation. Patrick Steven Yaroch, 37, used his investigative positions with access to FBI systems to steal cryptocurrency, then exchange and launder it through financial transactions to conceal its source and ownership. Yaroch made about 100 fraudulent transfers related to 35 FBI investigations, gaining $2,474,380.66 in proceeds, according to a news release from the US Attorney’s Office, Eastern District of Virginia on Thursday. He had earlier admitted to unauthorized transfers that involved about $1 million in digital assets, which was reported by Cointelegraph in August. Yaroch paid off his debts and intended to use the proceeds to finance a new life in Portugal, where he planned to buy a vineyard, according to the statement. The former agent admitted that his actions had compromised FBI investigations related to criminal groups and adversarial nations. Yaroch faces up to 20 years in prison. His sentencing is set for March 4, 2027. Magazine: AI agent disputes head to ‘Internet Court’ — and a jury of AI agents

items.titleTr: Bitcoin holders have received eCash — What can you do with it?
items.summaryTr: Bitcoin’s eCash fork gives eligible holders an equivalent balance of ECX, but questions remain over where they can trade the tokens and what they can do with them.
items.articleText: Bitcoin holders have received eCash — What can you do with it? Bitcoin’s eCash fork gives eligible holders an equivalent balance of ECX, but questions remain over where they can trade the tokens and what they can do with them. Somewhere between the Binance hack and the US midterms, Paul Sztorc’s long-awaited Bitcoin fork, known as the eCash network, went live. On Oct. 29, Sztorc, the founder of LayerTwo Labs and the driving force behind the Bitcoin Drivechain proposals BIP300 and BIP301 , launched a separate Bitcoin fork designed to bring payments, privacy and other applications to a network built from Bitcoin’s code. “We need to actively sabotage the ‘degrowth’ policies killing Bitcoin,” Sztorc tells Magazine. “We want to find the true Bitcoin builders and give them the tools to actually innovate. We just need the open-minded, risk-taking contrarians to come and build.” The hard fork gives eligible Bitcoin holders an interesting windfall: their equivalent BTC balance in the new chain’s native token, ECX. So what benefits does eCash bring to developers, and what can Bitcoin HODLers actually do with their new coins? What is eCash? Developed by Sztorc’s LayerTwo Labs, eCash is a separate hard fork of Bitcoin born out of Sztorc’s frustration with some of the “complacency narratives” and “cult-like toxicity” he believes has been holding Bitcoin back. Sztorc dismisses criticism of Drivechains’ security. Source: archive.ecash Its main innovation is Drivechains, a system that gives developers freedom to build independent sidechains with different features without having to make changes to Bitcoin’s base-layer protocol (or in this case, eCash’s base layer). Developers can experiment with different applications for payments, privacy, digital assets and prediction markets, and miners can “maximize their revenues” by earning additional transaction fees. Five sidechains launched alongside eCash’s mainnet: BitNames, BitAssets, Thunder, Truthcoin and zSide, with two more, the quantum-resistant Photon and decentralized exchange CoinShift, still to come. Related: Blockchain developer Paul Sztorc announces BTC hard fork eCash Sztorc has spent over a decade advocating for Drivechains and believes that Bitcoin’s notoriously conservative development approach has held back its potential. “Anything that isn’t maximizing network usage is simply a distraction,” he says. “Users, the ones who actually pay transaction fees to miners, will win in the long run.” Getting access to the new coins The eCash fork took place at Bitcoin block 973,728, and anyone who controlled their private keys at the snapshot received an equivalent ECX balance. “If you held the keys to your BTC at that exact block, you now own the exact same amount of ECX,” LayerTwo Labs tells Magazine. “It is that simple, and you can access them right now.” Like beauty, simplicity is in the eye of the beholder, and Bitcoiners who self-custody their coins will need to use a wallet that supports eCash and carefully follow its process to separate the ECX from their BTC. Because the two networks share transaction history, an unprotected transaction on one chain could be replayed on the other. eCash Market prices. Source: eCash. “Never move your BTC first, as an ordinary, unprotected BTC spend can easily be replayed on the ECX network,” LayerTwo Labs warns. Replay controls are built into the protocol, it says, but the company advises holders to move ECX first, before spending BTC. Anyone keeping BTC on a centralized exchange is “at their mercy regarding distribution,” and should check whether their exchange supports the fork or has announced an ECX distribution. Where can holders trade ECX? Accessing ECX isn’t the same thing as being able to sell it and the tokens are not yet widely available on larger crypto exchanges. Depending on which country you are in, there can be tax implications from Bitcoin forks, which are worth looking up before filing your next tax return. NeoxEX said it opened native ECX deposits, withdrawals and trading on Oct. 29, with ECX/USDT, ECX/USDC and ECX/BTC pairs, while CoinW announced plans to distribute ECX to eligible Bitcoin holders, with deposits, withdrawals and trading to be announced at a later date. Orca, a decentralized exchange on Solana, lets users swap USDC for wrapped ECX (wECX) through a liquidity pool. That gives holders another way to trade exposure to ECX, but it involves a wrapped token on a different blockchain rather than native ECX trading on the eCash network. Related: Binance, Polymarket seek Polygon hard fork to recover $6.8M in stolen crypto How much are the tokens worth? CoinMarketCap placed ECX at $32.63, with around $355,000 in 24-hour trading volume as of Nov. 5, while CoinGecko shows the token as a preview listing, with no price yet available and no tracked exchange markets. Crypto market data provider Kaiko says it does not track ECX, which limits the availability of independent market data. LayerTwo Labs says early trading saw ECX fluctuate between $40 and $50, but it did not provide supporting order book depth or trading volume figures, pointing instead to the Orca pool’s total value locked as a way for users to assess available liquidity. eCash is $32.63 on CoinMarketCap as of Nov. 5 “If our fork replicates even a fraction of [Bitcoin Cash] BCH’s initial performance,” Sztorc says, “the liquidity will be staggering,” adding that anyone concerned about low liquidity can hold their coins and decide later. “We are actively adding new exchanges and trading pairs, so the user experience will only improve,” he says. “Otherwise, you’re welcome to take your free money and leave.” A different vision for Bitcoin Sztorc says the value of eCash will ultimately depend on whether developers build useful applications and users are willing to pay for them. Paying customers and transaction fee revenue are the project’s main measures of success during its first year, he says. He’s not concerned about criticism of Drivechains’ security model, especially the “superstition” that miners could coordinate to steal funds held on sidechains. “If you genuinely believe miners will torch their own billion-dollar operations for a short-term theft on an L2, then you shouldn’t trust Bitcoin’s L1 either,” he says. So for now, eCash gives Bitcoiners a new asset and developers a new playground — but whether ECX becomes much more than that will depend on whether anyone actually wants to use it. Magazine: Bitcoin turns 18: Has the original rebel grown up?

items.title: CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation
items.verification: Birincil kaynak
items.titleTr: CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation
items.articleText: Release Number 9323-26 CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation November 05, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today issued an interpretation (“Interpretation”) of the requirement that designated contract markets (“DCMs”) provide competitive, open, fair, and impartial access to their members and persons with trading privileges under Commission Regulation 38.151(b) (“Impartial Access Requirements”). “Derivatives markets must operate on a uniform basis at a national scale in order to achieve the purposes set out in the Commodity Exchange Act,” said Chairman Michael S. Selig. “Geographic access restrictions are inconsistent with those purposes and the Act’s impartial access requirements.” DCMs must cease domestic geographic restrictions that violate the Impartial Access Requirements within 30 days, or else submit to the Division of Market Oversight (“Division”) an explanation for why such compliance is not feasible. Further, within 30 days, DCMs should ensure that intermediaries accessing their markets are not impeding and are complying with the DCM’s Impartial Access Requirements, or else submit to the Division an explanation for why such compliance is not feasible. The Commission will consider the facts and circumstances of any particular case in connection with potential Commission action. -CFTC-

Further, within 30 days, DCMs should ensure that intermediaries accessing their markets are not impeding and are complying with the DCM’s Impartial Access Requirements, or else submit to the Division an explanation for why such compliance is not feasible. The Commission will consider the facts and circumstances of any particular case in connection with potential Commission action. -CFTC-

items.articleText: Release Number 9322-26 CFTC Staff Addresses Use of Trust Companies for Daily Settlements November 05, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission’s Division of Clearing and Risk today issued a no-action letter addressing whether derivatives clearing organizations may use trust companies to conduct daily settlements with clearing members. According to the letter, a derivatives clearing organization may use a trust company for daily settlements if it treats the trust company as it would a settlement bank under applicable CFTC requirements. -CFTC-

items.title: CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets
items.verification: Birincil kaynak
items.titleTr: CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets
items.articleText: Release Number 9321-26 CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets November 04, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the U.S. Department of Agriculture today announced their signing of a Memorandum of Understanding intended to safeguard the integrity of U.S. agricultural markets. The MOU will allow the CFTC and USDA to harmonize policies and practices to better share information and increase access to risk management tools. The agreement will also assist both agencies with monitoring and identifying structural or potential systematic risks, among other things. “For decades, America’s agricultural community has relied on our markets to hedge risk, manage uncertainty, and plan for the future,” said CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig. “I’m proud that the CFTC and USDA have formalized this partnership through an MOU that will strengthen protections for America’s farmers, ranchers, and producers while expanding opportunities to manage risk through more efficient data sharing. I commend Secretary Rollins for her partnership and commitment to a more coordinated regulatory approach that safeguards the integrity of our markets and ensures they continue serving the agricultural community that feeds and clothes our nation.” “Faster and more transparent data sharing between USDA and CFTC is critical to helping our farmers and ranchers navigate an ever-changing market,” said USDA Secretary Brooke Rollins. “This MOU builds upon USDA’s ongoing data modernization efforts and allows our agencies to collaboratively identify risks and improve responses to market events. Breaking down barriers between government agencies to deliver for our customers is a hallmark of this administration and I am looking forward to the successes this MOU will bring.” -CFTC-

items.title: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud
items.verification: Birincil kaynak
items.titleTr: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud
items.articleText: Release Number 9320-26 CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud November 03, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Texas entered a default judgment against defendants Walter Dunning Larrick III and Cambridge Financial Advisors LLC for their participation in a commodities fraud scheme. In entering the default judgment, the court found the defendants fraudulently solicited and misappropriated more than $3 million from participants. The court found the defendants falsely represented they would use participant funds to trade futures and options, including those involving natural gas, oil, and gold; made material misrepresentations and omissions about the profitability of commodity trading with them; and issued false account statements to conceal their misconduct. The court further found the defendants misappropriated participant funds by making payments to existing participants in a manner akin to a Ponzi scheme, paying Larrick’s personal expenses, and sending funds to offshore accounts in Costa Rica. The court ordered the defendants to pay a $9,767,625 civil monetary penalty and $3,255,875 in restitution. It also permanently enjoined them from further violations of the Commodity Exchange Act and Commission regulations, as charged, and imposed permanent trading and registration bans. The default judgment resolves all claims in the CFTC’s 2023 complaint. [See CFTC Press Release No. 8768-23.] -CFTC-

items.title: CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures
items.verification: Birincil kaynak
items.titleTr: CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures
items.articleText: Release Number 9319-26 CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures November 03, 2026 WASHINGTON — CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig today released a statement announcing that perpetual futures contracts on individual equity securities can begin trading for the first time on designated contract markets that are dually registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission as notice-registered national securities exchanges to trade security futures products. Key excerpts from Chairman Selig’s statement: “Today, perpetual futures contracts on individual equity securities (the ‘Equity Perps’) can begin trading for the first time on CFTC-registered exchanges. … “This expansion marks a significant step towards allowing U.S. market participants, consistent with applicable law, to avail themselves of the advantages of perpetual futures that have led to their emergence as widely sought tools for risk-management and price-discovery. I believe that bringing these types of innovative products into our regulated markets ensures that American investors and traders can access these products within the protections of the CFTC’s proven regulatory framework, rather than being forced to turn to offshore, and often unregulated, venues. … “The Equity Perps build on the foundation of the [Commodity Futures Modernization Act of 2000] and the [CFTC-SEC Memorandum of Understanding]. For too long, regulatory uncertainty left innovative products, such as security futures and equity perpetual futures, stranded in what SEC Chairman Paul S. Atkins has aptly described as a regulatory ‘no man’s land’ due to a lack of harmonization between the agencies. The CFTC and SEC have turned the page on that era, and are committed to delivering regulatory clarity for innovative products and a clear path to market, rather than more casualties of jurisdictional disputes.” Read Chairman Selig’s full statement here. -CFTC-

items.title: CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
items.verification: Birincil kaynak
items.titleTr: CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
items.articleText: Release Number 9318-26 CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading October 28, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced it will host an industry roundtable Dec. 15 to discuss issues related to the viability of derivatives markets moving to 24/7 trading. The dialogue will build upon the CFTC’s Request for Comment earlier this summer on 24/7 trading. The CFTC’s roundtable will provide a public venue for dialogue on the evolving market structures shaping derivatives markets, including overnight trading, tokenization, infrastructure and staffing needs, and operational readiness. Participants will convene from across the industry to discuss how the Commission can promote responsible innovation while protecting market participants and preserving the integrity and resilience of U.S. derivatives markets. “I have been consistently clear: under my leadership, the CFTC will not take a one‑size‑fits‑all approach to 24/7 trading. Market structure evolves best through thoughtful and responsible progress, and that’s exactly why we’re hosting a roundtable to hear directly from industry on their views for 24/7 trading across different asset classes,” Chairman Selig said. The roundtable will take place at CFTC’s headquarters in Washington. Information regarding the agenda, speakers, and registration will be posted at a later date. This event will be open to the public and livestreamed on CFTC.gov. Please note the number of in-person participants may be limited, and visitors will be subject to security checks. Members of the public are welcome to submit speaker nominations to [email protected]. -CFTC-
